confidence_notes: The food and drink anchors are based on web search summaries of aggregator sites (Numbeo figures quoted by Nomad Watch, CityCost, MyLifeElsewhere, Whereandwhen, Expatistan and BorderlyAI). These sites mostly agree: an inexpensive meal costs about CNY 28-30, a mid-range dinner for two about CNY 180-300, a cappuccino about CNY 24-27 and a domestic draft beer about CNY 15-20. I converted CNY to USD at about 7.1 CNY per USD, which is an assumed rate from general knowledge, not one I searched. Beer is the restaurant-draft figure. Prices in tourist areas and pub-style bars are higher, often CNY 40-65 for a half-litre. The cocktail and wine figures are less reliable. I found no current Suzhou-specific aggregate for either, so they are estimates set above the beer price using benchmarks from mid-range bars in other Chinese cities (cocktails from about CNY 45-50, wine about CNY 50 a glass in Shanghai listings). Hotel bars charge much more. All accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge for July peak summer and were not checked against any booking sites or listings. The FX figure (0.6720 USD per AUD, 18 Nov 2026) came from a web search summary that quotes the RBA exchange-rate page and a secondary site repeating RBA data. I did not open the RBA page directly to confirm it.
comparable_city_reasoning: Suzhou is a wealthy tier-1.5 city in the Yangtze River Delta. Prices there are a bit below Shanghai and similar to Hangzhou and Nanjing. Aggregator comparisons put it about 40% above the Chinese national average, mainly because of restaurant prices. For accommodation, I assumed budget chain hotels and hostels in the old town and Pingjiang Road areas would cost about the same as in Hangzhou in summer.
